title: Why Vishnu keeps coming down
hook: Hiranyaksha blocks the way up, and three descents add up to one promise
carry: whenever dharma sinks, vishnu comes down
tomorrow: his brother wants revenge. what boon does he ask for?

segments.voice: Yesterday, avatar means God comes down to where we are, and the earth as Bhudevi: someone, not something, held like someone loved. But the one who sank the earth isn't done.

Every rescue story has a moment when the hero is almost home and someone steps into the doorway. Varaha is rising through the waters with the earth on his tusk, and there in the deep is Hiranyaksha, a demon who has been roaming the waters looking for someone strong enough to fight him. He mocks the boar. He has found his match.
screen: `ALMOST HOME.` → `HIRANYAKSHA IN THE DEEP.` → `A MATCH, AT LAST.`

segments.voice: In the Bhagavata Purana, Varaha doesn't drop the earth to answer him. He sets her safely on the water first, and only then turns to fight, and he defeats him. The Bhagavata gives this demon a surprising past: he and his brother were once Vishnu's own doorkeepers, Jaya and Vijaya, cursed by sages to be born for a time as his enemies. The brother is where the story goes next. Now step back and look at the three descents together. A fish, when the Vedas were lost in the flood. A tortoise, when the mountain sank. A boar, when the earth sank. Each time something holy is going under, and each time Vishnu comes down in the shape that can save it. Hindus have a word for what's going under: dharma, the right order of things, in the world and in a life. And they have Krishna's words for why he keeps coming, in the Bhagavad Gita. In paraphrase: whenever dharma declines and wrong rises, I come; to protect the good and set things right, I'm born age after age. That's why the avatars come in a row. It's one promise, kept in different shapes. And it's why, when a family's world seems to be sinking, many Hindus don't only ask for strength. They pray for Vishnu to come.
screen: `HIRANYAKSHA BLOCKS THE WAY UP.` · `THE EARTH SET DOWN SAFE FIRST.` · `FISH, TORTOISE, BOAR.` · `DHARMA SINKS. HE COMES DOWN.` · then, large: `ONE PROMISE, MANY SHAPES.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one of the three descents come back on its own: a fish in the flood, a tortoise under the mountain, a boar in the deep. Stay with whichever one comes, and breathe slowly. If you pray, ask Vishnu to come down to whatever is sinking in your week; if you don't, simply rest there.
Varaha: the boar who sets the earth down safe before he fights.
The line to take with you: whenever dharma sinks, Vishnu comes down. Fish, tortoise, boar.

howItsDone: Pictures of the Dashavatara, Vishnu's ten descents, are a familiar sight in Hindu homes and temples, and Varaha's fight with Hiranyaksha is told right before Narasimha, since the two demons are brothers.
